welcome.lead: Opencelium connects the systems you already run — Jira, Zendesk, SAP, HubSpot — and keeps their data in step.
welcome.body: You describe an API once, then wire methods together on a canvas. This tour walks the shortest path from nothing to a running workflow.

theme.body: The choice applies immediately. You can change it later in /ui/config, or with Ctrl + K → ui theme.
theme.lightDescription: Best in bright rooms and on projectors.
theme.darkDescription: Easier on the eyes for long log sessions.
theme.deviceDescription: Follows your system setting, including its schedule.

palette.body: It is highlighted behind this dialog. Press Ctrl + K from any screen to open it — you never have to reach for it with the mouse.

layers.body: Opencelium builds an integration in three layers, and each one needs the one before it. The next two steps set up the first layer.
layers.invoker: Describes an API: its endpoints, auth and request shapes. One file, reusable.
layers.connector: One real system: that invoker plus a base URL and credentials.
layers.workflow: The integration itself: methods of as many connectors as you need, wired on a canvas.

invoker.body: An invoker describes one API. Pick the quicker path unless your system is unusual.
invoker.uploadBody: Start from a template we ship, or a file your team already has. Jira, Zendesk, SAP and HubSpot are included.
invoker.manualBody: For an API we don't cover yet. You describe endpoints, auth and response shapes by hand — it takes longer.
invoker.existingBody: Your API descriptions are already available, so the upload task can be skipped.
invoker.commandHint: invoker upload — add an API description at any time

connector.generalBody: Two fields are required. The title is how you will recognise this system later; the invoker is the API description it speaks.
connector.title: Title
connector.credentialsBody: Fill the fields, then press Test connection. Opencelium calls the system once and tells you what came back.
connector.testFailed: Connection test failed. Check the credentials and try again.
connector.saveFailed: Connector could not be saved. Try again.
connector.warning: Credentials are encrypted at rest. If your install has a master password, the test asks for it once per session.
connector.nextBody: Systems your Jira data usually flows to:

checklist.title: Setup
checklist.dismissBody: It will not come back. You can still restart the tour from the palette with help onboarding, or turn it back on in /ui/config.

invoker.title: Add your first invoker
invoker.detail: Upload a description or write one.

integration.title: Finish the first integration
integration.detail: Connect two systems and schedule it.
